title: React kit: Pair with a Code, confirm and paired
summary: After the code is proven: the shower's 'Pair with LAPTOP-7QH3RX?' with what each of you shares (also with a 64-character and a right-to-left name), the joiner's 'Waiting for them to confirm', Paired with the name this device keeps (starting as the one the device sent), Paired while 8 devices can already connect, the shower back on its changed code after Not now or a timeout, and the joiner's Couldn't pair lines.
compare: 1: the prompt appears only after the other device proved the code, so 'It entered your code.' is true. The title is the name the other device sent (cleaned, not verified; often a hostname such as LAPTOP-7QH3RX), and 'Pair with this device?' when it sent none. Not now has first focus with the 250 ms guard (as LinkPairing), so Enter on arrival never pairs; Escape is Not now. Pair is the primary.

1b and 1c: the name is wrapped in <bdi>, wraps onto as many lines as it needs and is never truncated in this consent title (64 characters is the most a label keeps); a right-to-left name keeps the question mark at the end of the sentence.
2: the device that entered the code waits with 'Waiting for them to confirm' (linkPairing.waiting) and 'Pairing with Studio PC.'; Cancel ends it for both. 120 seconds to confirm.

3: the success check in the logo's place, 'Paired' (Title Case, the done state's name) and 'You can now connect on the same network without a code.' The Name field starts with the name the device sent (LAPTOP-7QH3RX), which is what makes renaming here worth having; editing it renames the device on this device only ('Shown on this device only.'), and Done saves it.

4: when 8 paired devices can already connect, the new one is kept with Can connect off and a neutral notice says 'LAPTOP-7QH3RX can't connect' / 'Only 8 paired devices can connect at once. Turn one off in Paired devices.', with Paired devices beside Done.

5: on the device that showed the code, Not now, a timeout or a closed connection never ends the window while it is open: it returns to the code screen with the changed code (the first two digits kept, the rest lit) and a neutral notice under the time, 'Not paired with LAPTOP-7QH3RX.' / 'The code changed.' (R1 reason declined, timeout or closed). 'Couldn't pair' appears there only once the window has closed (sdk.react-pair-show 5, 5c).

6: the device that entered the code shows 'Couldn't pair' (sentence case) with one line: someone said Not now, time ran out, one device has no room, or the connection closed (R9 tells them apart), then Try again (back to the field, with sdk.react-pair-enter 3's rules) and Close.
Four sizes: three windows a row at wide and desktop; 5 across two columns beside the Couldn't pair card; two a row at tablet; stacked on phone.
Accent, type and radii match sdk.react-activate: Polaris look by default, DJDL's coral accent, no Polaris Key or Polaris Locker words or marks anywhere (there is no account in this flow).
Words are the copyKeys below, verbatim ('revised' marks a key this round added or changed; 'was' is the old value); no 'CPace', 'nameplate', 'mode', 'link secret' or 'local link' reaches a person.

copyKeys.note: Shower, after the code is proven. Arguments: {device} = the label the other device sent (cleaned, not verified), in <bdi>, never truncated.
When the other device sent no label.
Declines; first focus with the 250 ms guard; Escape. Nothing is stored and the code changes.
The done state's name (LOCKER-FEATURE-NAMES); same value as linkPairing.linkedTitle. Add to TITLE_CASE_KEYS.

sdkNeeds.need: Shower: each onCode carries a reason (opened, wrong-code, declined, timeout, closed) and LocalCode.expiresAt, so every kit's ring agrees and a decline is not shown as a wrong code.
Joiner: a typed end that tells declined, timeout and closed apart (today all three are peer-closed); it picks failedDeclined, failedTimeout or failedClosed.
List: a public onChange(fn), firing on pair, rename, forget, setReachable, lastSeen writes and gate flips.

platforms.react: Electron over Node: show, enter and manage; no scanning. In a browser or a desktop-bridge page there is no local network (connect-unavailable), so the kit renders nothing and the host shows no entry.
platforms.swiftui: iOS and iPadOS: scan first, then show, enter and manage (sdk.swiftui-pair-scan: AVFoundation, the kit's own viewfinder); the app declares NSCameraUsageDescription and the Local Network keys. macOS: show, enter and manage, no scanning, as the React boards.
platforms.compose: Android: scan first, then show, enter and manage. The Play flavour opens Google's code scanner (its own UI, no camera permission), so sdk.swiftui-pair-scan 2, 3 and 3c are iOS only; because Google's scanner cannot show the categories, its choose screen (1) shows 'Each of you shares' and the pills under Scan a code before the scanner opens. A build without Play services has no Scan a code and types the code. Desktop: show, enter and manage.
platforms.godot: Show (QR from ui/qr/), enter and manage; no scanning. Two panes by its own two_pane_fits() rule.

designReview.verdict: Fix (good): clean and well judged; the shower's state after Not now, a timeout or a closed connection contradicted the SDK, which keeps the window open with a new code. Fixed in one follow-up.

findings.issue: The shower's terminal 'Couldn't pair' card contradicted localShower.ts, which rotates the code and keeps the window open.
findings.resolution: 5: the shower returns to its changed code with 'Not paired with LAPTOP-7QH3RX.' / 'The code changed.' (R1). 'Couldn't pair' is used there only once the window has closed; the joiner keeps the card (6) with Try again back to the field (R9).

findings.issue: The shower saw LAPTOP-7QH3RX but Paired's name field showed Theo's laptop; no long or right-to-left label was drawn.
findings.resolution: Name prefilled with LAPTOP-7QH3RX; 1b draws a 64-character label and 1c a Hebrew one, in <bdi>, wrapping, never truncated.

findings.issue: '{device} can't connect yet' promised a change that will not happen by itself.
findings.resolution: 'LAPTOP-7QH3RX can't connect' / 'Only 8 paired devices can connect at once. Turn one off in Paired devices.'
Escape is Not now; Not now keeps first focus and the 250 ms guard.
Sentence case (a statement); failedTitle leaves the plan's Title Case list.
